items.title: Lizzie Miles Interview, 1951-01-18
items.q: And this Perry Bradford who had discovered Mamie Smith, he was then working on Edith Wilson.

ctx.x: You mean here in the city? Yes. No, no. I didn't. I didn't. I just came and visited with my mother, you know. And then I went back. I went back to Chicago. And when I went back to Chicago, there was a producer around there, Jerry Mills, a stage producer, putting on shows. And he had a job for me in Springfield, Illinois, in a cabaret there. And I went. There was a great. He's a great pianist now, but I can't think of his name that I met there. And he was a young fellow just starting then, you know, playing in…

if I was gonna make any money, you know. And so he told me, well, the idea was he had the telegram. He showed me the telegram from the Victor in the Columbia, telling him to bring a blues singer for audition, you know. And so he said, I would get all my transportation paid and everything, and I told him, could I get an advance? I wanted to make sure. So he said, yes, he asked me what I wanted, I told him. And so then I said, well, I'd go, and I went to New York and made a test for the Columbia and the OK, and…

I wanted to ask you a few questions about your phonograph record. I know this is going to be kind of hard on your memory. But do you remember who you made Grieving Mama Blues and Slow Up Papa with? Oh, that's on the OK. With Piana and Cornette.
